title: why-we-killed-our-redis-cluster
summary: How we replaced an over-engineered $900/month managed cluster with local SQLite read replicas, simpler code, and zero 2 AM pager alerts.

children.text: For two years, our engineering team treated Redis like magical pixie dust. Whenever an endpoint was sluggish, someone would say: 'Just stick it in Redis.' Before long, we had 42 distinct cache keys, five background eviction cron jobs, and an architecture nobody fully understood.

Cache invalidation isn't just hard—it is a relentless source of subtle, user-facing bugs. When our inventory counts went out of sync during a flash sale, we realized our caching layer was hiding poor database indexing instead of actually solving performance.

We deleted 80% of the cache keys. We properly indexed our PostgreSQL tables, added partial indexes for active tenants, and used local in-memory LRU caches with strict 10-second TTLs for hot reads. Total latency dropped, and our infrastructure cost plummeted.
